findings.issue: contradicts task clause: the description's fault is 'the report's date inputs render the host placeholder (dd. mm. 2026.) in committed shots', and the task title says committed images 'carry no host format'. The diff pins Intl/Date/navigator.language/number format, but not the native <input type=date> placeholder, which is the one symptom the clause names. I reproduced the limit read-only (in-memory element screenshots, nothing written): on this host (AppleLocale en_US@rg=rszzzz) a bare date input hashes identically under context locale en-US and de-DE with --lang=en-US, and differs only under --lang=de-DE. So the limit is real and the executor's disclosure is accurate. But the disclosure lives only in a code comment: the non-check capture that writes the PNGs prints nothing, and shot()'s pinProblem cannot see the placeholder (it is not in the DOM). A maintainer regenerating shots on such a host commits host-shaped 'filters' / date-input pixels with every check green and a 'pinned' label that now over-claims.
findings.resolution: Make the residual visible at the moment it matters instead of only in a comment. Options, structurally preferred first: (a) in the writing path of shot() (not --check), on darwin read the OS regional format (`defaults read -g AppleLocale`, region suffix `@rg=` other than US) and refuse, or at least print a loud note naming the shots that contain a native date input; (b) add the same reading to machineFingerprint() so --repro and the provenance line quote it. Node's own Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale is NOT usable for this: it reports en-US on the overridden host. Alternatively file the date-placeholder half as its own open task/fault so it is tracked rather than documented-away.

findings.issue: The pinned-context assertion runs inside shot(), so a leg that never reaches shot() (e.g. the ladderCtx / prioCtx pages at 7340 and 7415, which drive checks without a shutter) is pinned by option only and unasserted. Today harmless, since they produce no image.
findings.resolution: No action needed unless those contexts ever begin to photograph; if they do, they pass through shot() and are covered. Optionally note this in the PINNED_CONTEXT comment.

intent.note: Clause quoted: 'capture-screenshots.mjs sets no locale/timezone; the report's date inputs render the host placeholder (dd. mm. 2026.) in committed shots'. Diff half 1 (sets locale/timezone): done - PIN_LOCALE/PIN_TIMEZONE on 9 newContext sites (grep 'locale: PIN_LOCALE'), --lang=en-US on launch (tools/capture-screenshots.mjs:7039), asserted in shot() before the shutter and before the --check return, with a de-DE/Asia/Tokyo negative control (assertPinDetectorRejects). Diff half 2 (date-input placeholder no longer host-shaped): NOT achieved on a host with an OS regional override; I confirmed by probe that no context-level lever moves it. The executor's outcome describes the diff accurately and says so ('documented not fixed'), so the claim matches the diff; it is the task's headline symptom that the diff leaves open. The only remaining mitigation is findings 1. I ran `node tools/capture-screenshots.mjs --check` once in the task tree: exit 0, and the run emitted the control note 'context pin: a de-DE / Asia/Tokyo context is rejected, so the check can fail'. No PNGs were regenerated, so committed shots still carry the old placeholder until the orchestrator re-captures.
